name: Nasir Khusraw's seven-year journey
traveler: Nasir Khusraw, a tax official of Merv
summary: After a dream tells him to give up wine, a Persian civil servant sets out for Mecca and is gone seven years. He describes Jerusalem before the Crusades, Fatimid Cairo at its richest, and the Qarmatian republic of al-Hasa in eastern Arabia, then returns by way of Basra and Isfahan.

stops.note: He resigns his post and sets out, with his brother and a slave.
He meets the poet Qatran and explains the hard words in his verses.
Its black basalt walls, which he measures.
Into Syria, where tolls are paid on goods from Byzantium, Egypt and Iraq.
Down the coast through Tripoli, Beirut and Acre.
He describes the Dome of the Rock and the city fifty years before the Crusaders take it.
Three years in the Fatimid capital: twenty thousand shops, the caliph's palaces and the opening of the canal at the Nile flood.
Up the Nile to the edge of Nubia.
Across the desert to the Red Sea port.
His last pilgrimage, then east across Arabia.
The Qarmatian state of al-Hasa, ruled by a council, where no one pays taxes and loans carry no interest.
He arrives in rags and is turned out of the bathhouse; a fresh suit wins him a welcome.
The finest city he has seen in Persian lands.

informs.note: Fatimid Cairo from three years inside it
